product.intro: App Launchpad is a GitHub template for starting a project and shipping reviewed changes.
sections: Start a project
Create a repository from the template, record the template version, and agree on one user workflow before selecting services.
Review a change
Open an issue with the intended outcome and acceptance criteria. Link the implementation PR and use its checks to see what was verified.

technical.intro: The template provides repository tooling and a static site. Generated projects choose their own application stack.
sections: Repository checks
Python scripts validate project metadata, repository links, and the public documentation build. GitHub Actions runs those checks through the foundation workflow.
Publication
GitHub Releases stores tagged template versions. GitHub Pages can publish the curated site once enabled on the repository.

settings.intro: App Launchpad has repository configuration. It has no in-app settings panel.
sections: GitHub Pages
The repository owner enables Pages and selects GitHub Actions as the publishing source. Publication runs from the default branch.
Repository protection
Repository maintainers set the required check and review policy. The foundation check is the template baseline. Update the policy when the project adds its own application checks.
Settings in generated apps
For each real setting, document its default, who can change it, whether it applies to one account or the whole workspace, and when changes take effect.

sdlc.intro: The software development life cycle takes a change from an issue to a verified release.
sections: Plan and implement
Set the expected outcome in an issue. Work on a short-lived branch. Update the affected product, technical, settings, or delivery guide in the same PR.
Review and release

Record the documentation decision and test evidence in the PR. The template uses a checked implementation PR to the default branch. Applications with deployed pre-production verify the release candidate there before a separate promotion PR.
Verify the result
Confirm the published tag or live revision. Verify public documentation separately and record where recovery instructions live.

pipeline.intro: Follow the GitHub Actions stages from proposed change to published documentation.
stages: The foundation check validates the documentation decision, builds the public site and checks internal links alongside the repository tests.
The maintainer reviews the current evidence and merges the approved PR into the default branch.
On an eligible default-branch change, the Pages workflow builds the curated artifact and publishes it if Pages is enabled.
Open the live guides and check the expected revision and changed links.
sections: When a check fails
Fix the issue in the PR and check the new revision. If a Pages job fails after merge, review that publishing run and verify the live docs separately.
